transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... I hope it's okay that I'm here, I might just be overthinking things. But, well, I work as an insurance claims clerk, and... I guess the main thing that pushed me to finally make an appointment is that I just keep getting up from my workstation during the day. 

Like, I know I’m supposed to stay put and just finish my claim reviews, but I keep finding little reasons to walk away from my desk. It's probably just a bad habit, really. I try so hard to be a good employee and do what's expected of me, but... I figured I should probably ask a professional about it before it becomes a bigger issue at work. Is that... is that the kind of thing you can help with?
Can you describe what goes through your mind when you get up from your workstation? Are you feeling like you have to do it, or is it more of a choice?

Um, well, it's not like I feel forced to get up, exactly. It's more like... I just think of something else I should probably do. Like, maybe I need to grab a glass of water, or I suddenly remember I should check the printer for a document, even if I don't really need it right that second. 

It feels like a choice, I guess? I mean, I know I *should* just sit there and focus, and I really do try. I'm not trying to be difficult or avoid my work, I promise. It's just... my mind kind of wanders, and then before I know it, I'm standing up. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right. I just don't want you to think I'm slacking off on purpose.
Do you ever have thoughts that bother you or come into your mind uninvited, even if you're not acting on them?

Um, no, I don't think I really experience anything quite like that. I mean, my mind definitely wanders a lot, like I was saying, but the thoughts aren't... they aren't bad or upsetting, if that makes sense. 

It's mostly just random, harmless things, like, um, remembering I need to buy groceries or wondering if I replied to an email. Nothing that really bothers me or feels scary or anything. I hope that's okay? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right and giving you the information you need.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about things, even when there doesn’t seem to be a clear reason for it?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I care about doing a good job and being responsible, of course. I want to make sure I'm doing things right, but I don't think I worry excessively or... or for no reason. 

I guess I might stress a little bit if I fall behind on my claim reviews because I got distracted, but I think that's pretty normal, right? Like, anyone would feel a little anxious if they weren't meeting their quotas. But I don't just sit around worrying about random things out of nowhere. I hope that's a good thing? I'm trying my best to just be mindful of my work and not overcomplicate things.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, even outside of work?

Um, no, not at all. I mean, I actually have a pretty good mood most of the time. I still really enjoy my hobbies when I have the time for them. I like playing video games with my friends and, um, watching movies. 

I definitely don't feel hopeless or anything like that. I know I struggle a bit with staying on track at work, but I'm really trying to get better at it, and I feel positive about figuring it out. I'm generally a pretty upbeat person, I think. Is that what you were looking for? I just want to reassure you that I'm not depressed or anything, I'm just trying to get a handle on my focus.
Do you often feel restless or find yourself moving around more than usual, like you can't sit still or need to be constantly doing something?

Um, I guess maybe a little bit? But I don't think it's anything extreme or, you know, disruptive. Like, I don't get up and walk around when I'm not supposed to. 

It's more just... well, if I'm in a long training session or one of our bigger team meetings, I might, um, bounce my leg a bit under the table. Or I'll catch myself clicking my pen or just sort of shifting around in my chair. I really try to look focused and pay attention, I promise. It's just a way to kind of keep myself alert when things drag on, I think. A lot of people do that, right? I hope it doesn't make me seem unprofessional or anything. I always try to be respectful of whoever is speaking.
Do you often find yourself losing track of what you're supposed to be doing, even in the middle of a task, or do you tend to get easily sidetracked by things around you?

Um, well, I guess I do get a little sidetracked sometimes, but I really try not to let it affect my work too much. Like, if I'm reviewing a policy and, um, someone nearby starts talking about a different claim, or if I just suddenly remember I need to pick up dry cleaning or something... my attention kind of just slides away from what I'm reading. 

I usually catch it pretty quickly, though! I just have to, you know, go back and reread the same section a few times to make sure I actually absorbed it. I really want to be thorough and not make any mistakes on the claims. It's just a little blip in focus, I think. Does that make sense? I hope that doesn't sound too bad. I always make sure the work gets done right in the end.
Do you often find yourself overlooking small details or making careless mistakes in your work, even when you're trying to stay focused?

Um, well, I guess everyone makes a little typo here and there, right? I really, really try to be careful. I know how important accuracy is with insurance claims, so I always double-check my work. 

Sometimes, if I've been looking at the screen for a really long time, maybe I'll transpose a number in a policy code, or, um, miss a tiny check box on a form. But it's not like I'm just rushing through it carelessly! I always want to do a good job. And usually, the system catches those little things anyway, or I catch them when I review it. I really hope that doesn't make me sound incompetent. I'm actually very dedicated to getting things right, I just... maybe my eyes get a little tired sometimes? Is that a normal thing to happen?
Looking back, did you have similar issues with staying focused or being easily distracted when you were a child, like in school or during homework?

Um, well... I guess if I really think about it, it's not exactly a brand new thing. But I wasn't a bad kid or anything! I was actually pretty smart, I promise. 

I just... well, in elementary school, my teachers would sometimes write on my report cards that I was bright, but maybe a little disorganized? Like, I guess I used to lose my worksheets sometimes, or, um, miss part of the instructions when they were explaining things. And they'd have to remind me to finish my classwork instead of just staring out the window. But I think a lot of kids are like that, right? Just a little daydreamy? I always meant well, and I did try my best to be a good student. I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a troublemaker or lazy. I really wasn't.

Can you recall if these issues with focus or restlessness tend to happen more when you're in situations where you're supposed to remain seated or stay quiet, like in meetings or during training sessions?

Um, well, I guess... I mean, I try really hard to be respectful and pay attention during those things. I know the trainings are important. 

But, um, if it's a really long team meeting or something, I might get just a tiny bit restless? Not disruptive, though! I'm always quiet. I just... I might bounce my leg a little bit under the table, or, you know, click my pen. Sometimes I just have to keep shifting around in my chair to get comfortable. I really do try to look like I'm focused, and I *am* listening, I promise. It's just hard to sit completely still for that long. I think a lot of people probably get a little fidgety in long meetings, don't they? I hope my supervisor doesn't think I'm not paying attention, because I really am trying my best to be a good employee.
Do you find yourself getting distracted or having trouble staying still in situations outside of work, like when you're at home trying to relax or spending time with friends?

Um, no, not really. I mean, when I'm at home or with my friends, I'm usually pretty relaxed. I don't think I'm jumping around or anything like that. 

I guess... well, sometimes if we're watching a really long movie, I might get up to grab a snack or check my phone a few times, but that's just normal, right? Everyone likes to stretch their legs. And with my friends, we're usually doing something active anyway, or just hanging out, so it's not like I have to sit perfectly still. I really try to be a good listener when they're talking to me, and I think I'm a pretty attentive friend. I don't think I'm hyper or anything outside of work. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering this right.
Do you ever feel like you have to do certain things a particular way, like checking or redoing tasks, even if you know it's not really necessary?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I try to be careful with my work because I process insurance policies and I want to make sure I'm doing a good job. So I'll double-check things to make sure I didn't miss a detail or make a mistake, but it's just because I want to be thorough, you know? 

I don't feel like I *have* to do it in a weird way or anything. I just want to be a reliable employee. I'm definitely not doing things over and over for no reason. Just regular checking to make sure it's right. That's a good thing, right? Being careful with important documents? I just want to make sure I'm doing things the way I'm supposed to.

Do you ever find yourself struggling to stay focused or feeling restless in situations that aren’t work-related, like when you’re reading a book, watching something, or talking with someone one-on-one?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I try really hard to give people my full attention when we're talking one-on-one. I think it's important to be polite and listen, you know? 

If I'm reading or watching something, I guess... well, I might lose my place in a book sometimes if I've been reading for a long time, but I think that happens to everyone when they get a little tired, right? I just go back and reread the page. And if I'm watching a show, I'm usually pretty good about it. I might look at my phone for a second, but I'm still paying attention to the story. I don't feel restless or anything like that. I really do try to stay focused on whatever I'm supposed to be doing. That's pretty normal, isn't it?
